CONCLUSIONS AND RECOMMENDATIONS The KCL polymer mud system proved very effective in drilling this section which included the GUMBO type NORDLAND clays. A KCL level of 45-50ppb was necessary to inhibit the clays present and high level of dilution was required to keep the MBT below 25ppb. Above this level the rheology became very difficult to control. The KCL level had been allowed to deplete after entering the chalk and it was 25ppb when the Valhall mudstone was drilled. This formation gave tight hole conditions when it was being drilled and on subsequent trips. It may be possible to reduce some of the drag by maintaining the KCL level at 3Oppb below the chalk. This may be too high and could aggravate tight hole problems if the hole is left open for long period.
